subject: dsa
title: Number of 1 Bits
summary: Repeatedly apply n & (n - 1), which erases the lowest set bit each time. Count how many times you can do it before n reaches 0 — that's the number of 1-bits.
problem: Return the number of set bits (the Hamming weight) in the binary representation of an unsigned integer.

steps.caption: Count the 1-bits in 11, which is 1011 in binary. Trick: n & (n - 1) erases the lowest set bit, so count how many times we can do that.
The lowest set bit is the final 1. Subtracting 1 gives 1010; AND-ing it with n clears exactly that bit.
n becomes 1010. That is one bit cleared, so count = 1.
Repeat: the lowest set bit is now bit 1. Clearing it gives 1000, count = 2.
Once more: clear the top bit, so 1000 becomes 0000 and count = 3. Now n is 0, so stop.
We erased a bit three times, so 11 has three 1-bits.
